subject: Unit economics benchmarking: hosted baseline -> Dedicated / Private deltas

Cc: FinApp Procurement <procurement@finapp.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on baseline hosted pricing + what changes if we go Dedicated/Private

Jordan — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to capture a single-sheet view comparing the hosted API baseline unit economics to Dedicated (reserved) and Private (VPC / on-prem) options. Specifically they want: 
- per-token baseline (hosted) and how that maps to per-token or per-hour under Dedicated
- which cost components drop vs which new ones appear (e.g., infra ops, support, licensing, network egress)
- any minimum commits, setup fees, or infra migration lift to account for
- an example for our 1B tokens/month projection and a 50M tokens/month pilot

Can you share a short benchmarking spreadsheet and a quick note on assumptions? Procurement timeline is ~2–3 weeks.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Platform Product
FinApp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Coulter <evan@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on baseline hosted pricing + what changes if we go Dedicated/Private

Hi Evan — great to hear from you. Attaching a compact workbook that walks through: hosted baseline (per-1k tokens), conversion to reserved GPU-hour economics for Dedicated, and a Private deployment example that includes one-time setup + ongoing platform fee. Highlights up front: 

- Hosted: straightforward per-token pricing; no infra ops for you, predictable at low monthly commitment.
- Dedicated: shifts to a combination of reserved GPU capacity (monthly commit) + per-token marginal for burst; unit cost usually drops ~25–40% at 1B tokens/month depending on model selection and batching.
- Private: biggest changes are fixed platform + support fees, potential infra egress and KMS/HSM costs; unit token cost can be similar to Dedicated at scale but there is a non-trivial onboarding amortization (3–6 months).

I pulled together two worked examples in the sheet (50M and 1B tokens) with conservative batching and a mid-tier model profile. See attachment: redwood-unit-econ-compare-2027Q3.xlsx

Quick question for procurement so we align assumptions: do you expect to host the Private deployment on an existing FinApp VPC/cloud account (we’ll need exact region and instance types), or would you prefer Redwood-managed infra for the pilot? That changes the infra egress assumptions.

Next steps: happy to run a live walkthrough with your procurement + infra folks. Available Wed 10–11am PT or Thu 2–3pm PT.

— Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick question on baseline hosted pricing + what changes if we go Dedicated/Private

Marissa —
Quick reply: typical commercial guidance for 1B tokens/month: 
- Hosted baseline: list price used in sheet (0.9¢/1k) with standard commit discounts up to 15% for multi-quarter prepay.
- Dedicated: recommend 20–35% unit delta vs hosted at 1B depending on model/quantization + reserved GPU sizing. Use 30% conservatively in the sheet.
- Private: economics similar to Dedicated after amortizing onboarding (we typically model 6 months onboarding amortized over 12 months in the workbook). Add a platform fee (one-time) in the $40k–$120k band depending on features (KMS, HSM, extended retention).
- Onboarding/setup: $25k flat for a standard VPC install; more if air-gapped on-prem.

Lauren — please add a row for 'migration engineering estimate' (hours) to the spreadsheet — FinApp will want to know lift.

-Ben
